mainTopic: How ״יִטְמָא״ teaches the spread of טומאה through food and liquids, and how רבי יוסי and רבי עקיבא differ on levels of טומאה
overview: The גמרא first asks why the טומאה of משקין that touched a שרץ is not simply learned from a קל וחומר. It answers with the rule of דיו: a law learned through a קל וחומר is no stricter than its source. Next, a ברייתא explains that the first ״יִטְמָא״ in the פסוק teaches that אוכל makes משקין impure. A קל וחומר rules out a כלי, and משקין are an exception because they catch טומאה without a הכשר. The גמרא then asks why the rule that טומאה does not pass to a similar item is taught twice. It answers that one פסוק covers liquids made impure by a שרץ and the other covers liquids made impure by a כלי, and that the Torah sometimes writes out what a קל וחומר could teach. רבינא then challenges רב אשי by quoting רבא: רבי יוסי and רבי עקיבא disagree with each other. רב אשי answers that רבי יוסי was only speaking according to his teacher רבי עקיבא. Finally, רב אשי brings a ברייתא showing רבי יוסי's own approach. In it, שלישי בקודש comes from the Torah and רביעי בקודש comes from a קל וחומר. The פסוק for שלישי begins at the end of the amud and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Can't this be learned from a logical argument?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the טומאה of משקין that touched a שרץ could come from a קל וחומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Doesn't this come from a קל וחומר? If liquids that became impure because of a כלי make other things impure, then liquids that became impure because of a שרץ should certainly do so too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the current approach. It points out that a simple logical argument (a קל וחומר) seems to give us this law about liquids that touched a שרץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כלי is only impure because a שרץ touched it, so the שרץ is the stronger source of טומאה. If liquids impure through the weaker source spread טומאה, then liquids impure through the stronger source should spread it at least as much, and maybe more.

keyTerms.meaning: An argument from a lighter case to a stricter case
It comes (is derived)
Liquids
Because of, due to
A creeping creature whose dead body causes טומאה
All the more so

phrases.english: And doesn't it come from a kal vachomer:

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה מַשְׁקִין הַבָּאִין מֵחֲמַת כְּלִי — מְטַמְּאִין,
phrases.english: just as liquids that come (to impurity) because of a vessel transmit impurity,
phrases.notes: The כלי itself became impure from a שרץ.

phrases.aramaic: מַשְׁקִין הַבָּאִין מֵחֲמַת שֶׁרֶץ — לֹא כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן!
phrases.english: liquids that come (to impurity) because of a creeping animal, all the more so!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of how רבי עקיבא learns the טומאה of liquids.
steps.kashyaTarget: How the law of liquids that touched a שרץ is derived, and how strict that law is
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Liquids impure from the weaker source (a כלי) spread טומאה, so liquids impure from the stronger source (a שרץ) should spread it as well, and perhaps even more.
steps.confusionAlert: The liquids here became impure in two different ways. Some got their טומאה from a כלי, and others got it directly from a שרץ. Keep the two straight.

steps.title: The rule of 'it is enough'
steps.stepSummary: The rule of דיו: a law learned from a קל וחומר is no stricter than its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is enough for what is learned from the argument to be like the case it was learned from.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a famous rule. A קל וחומר can teach a law, but it cannot make that law stricter than the case it came from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Yes, the liquids that touched a שרץ do spread טומאה because of the קל וחומר. However, because of דיו, they spread it only to the same degree as liquids that became impure through a כלי, and no more.

keyTerms.meaning: It is enough for it
The law that comes from the logical argument
The source case being compared

steps.whatToRemember: דיו לבא מן הדין להיות כנדון: a קל וחומר can never produce a law stricter than its source.
steps.whyThisMatters: דיו is a basic tool used all over ש״ס to limit what a קל וחומר can teach.

phrases.english: It is sufficient for that which comes from the inference
to be like the source case.

steps.triggerLanguage: דַּיּוֹ לַבָּא מִן הַדִּין לִהְיוֹת כַּנִּדּוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by agreeing that the קל וחומר works, but limiting how far it reaches.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Liquids that touched a שרץ might be even stricter than liquids that touched a כלי.
steps.terutzMaskana: They are only as strict as liquids that touched a כלי, because of דיו.

steps.title: How is the first 'shall be impure' explained?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי עקיבא explains the word ״יִטְמָא״ in the first part of the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does he explain the word 'shall be impure' in the first part of the verse?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to a new question and sets up the next step. רבי עקיבא used the word ״יִטְמָא״ from the end of the פסוק, so what does he learn from the same word at the beginning?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says ״יִטְמָא״ twice. One appears about food and one about liquids. Each word should teach something, so the גמרא needs a lesson for the first one.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall be impure (read here as 'shall make impure')
Of the first part
How does he explain it?

phrases.english: 'Shall be impure' of the first part, how does he interpret it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the second ״יִטְמָא״ to the first one in the same פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What lesson רבי עקיבא learns from the first ״יִטְמָא״ in ויקרא 11:34

steps.title: Food makes liquids impure
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains that the first ״יִטְמָא״ teaches that food makes liquids impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Of all food which may be eaten, upon which water comes, shall be impure.' 'Shall be impure' means it makes liquids impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by quoting a ברייתא. It reads ״יִטְמָא״ as 'it shall make impure' and says impure food makes liquids impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word is read actively, as something the food does to other things. That turns it from describing the food's own status into a rule about how food spreads טומאה to liquids.

keyTerms.meaning: May be eaten
To make impure
Food

phrases.english: 'Of all food which may be eaten
upon which water comes, shall be impure,'
'shall be impure' means to make the liquids impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכׇּל הָאֹכֶל אֲשֶׁר יֵאָכֵל אֲשֶׁר יָבוֹא עָלָיו מַיִם יִטְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the first ״יִטְמָא״.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It teaches that impure food makes liquids impure.

steps.title: Maybe it means food makes a vessel impure
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks whether the word could instead teach that food makes a כלי impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you say it means to make liquids impure, or perhaps it only means to make a vessel impure?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא challenges its own reading. Why say the word refers to liquids, when it could refer to a כלי?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ״יִטְמָא״ does not say what the food makes impure. So the ברייתא has to rule out other options, and a כלי is the obvious alternative.

keyTerms.meaning: You say
Or perhaps it is only
A vessel or utensil

phrases.english: You say it means to make the liquids impure,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא לְטַמֵּא אֶת הַכְּלִי?
phrases.english: or perhaps it means only to make the vessel impure?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתָּה אוֹמֵר לְטַמֵּא אֶת הַמַּשְׁקִין, אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא לְטַמֵּא אֶת הַכְּלִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the reading just given.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that ״יִטְמָא״ refers to liquids
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק does not say what is made impure, so it could just as easily mean a כלי.

steps.title: A logical argument rules out the vessel
steps.stepSummary: A קל וחומר shows that food cannot make a כלי impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can make a קל וחומר: liquid makes food impure, yet it does not make a vessel impure. Food does not even make other food impure, so surely it should not make a vessel impure!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers with a קל וחומר. It proves that food cannot make a כלי impure, so the word cannot mean that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Liquid is stronger than food, because liquid makes food impure and food does not. If even the stronger liquid cannot make a כלי impure, the weaker food certainly cannot.

keyTerms.meaning: You can say (argue)
Liquid
Is it not logical?

phrases.english: You can say a kal vachomer:
just as liquid, which makes food impure,
does not make a vessel impure,
food, which does not make food impure,
is it not logical that it should not make a vessel impure?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the 'vessel' option raised in the previous step.
steps.terutzResolutionType: קל וחומר that rules out the alternative
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ״יִטְמָא״ might teach that food makes a כלי impure.
steps.terutzMaskana: Food cannot make a כלי impure, because even the stronger liquid cannot.

steps.title: The word refers to liquids, which become impure easily
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא concludes that ״יִטְמָא״ teaches that food makes liquids impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: So how do I explain 'shall be impure'? It means making liquids impure, since they easily pick up impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא wraps up. With the כלי ruled out, the word must mean that food makes liquids impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Liquids are especially quick to become impure. So even though food is too weak to make a כלי impure, it is strong enough to make liquids impure.

keyTerms.meaning: So how do I explain (fulfill) the verse?
Prone, likely
To receive (pick up) impurity

steps.whatToRemember: According to this ברייתא, food makes liquids impure but does not make a כלי impure. Liquids are an exception because they pick up טומאה very easily.

phrases.english: So how do I fulfill 'shall be impure'?
To make the liquids impure,
which are prone to receive impurity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion now that the alternative has been rejected.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The first ״יִטְמָא״ teaches that food makes liquids impure, because liquids are especially prone to טומאה.

steps.title: Why mention that liquids are susceptible?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי עקיבא's reasoning. Why give the reason 'liquids are susceptible to טומאה' when a simpler reason exists: there is nothing else left for food to make impure?
steps.simpleTranslation: Why mention liquids specifically 'because they are susceptible to impurity'? Let him derive it simply from the fact that there is nothing else for food to make impure!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions an extra reason in the ברייתא. It wants to know why רבי עקיבא explained 'food makes liquids impure' by saying liquids are susceptible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא already showed that food cannot make a כלי impure, and food does not make other food impure. So liquids are the only option left. The extra reason about liquids being 'susceptible' looks unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: Why specifically this? (asks why a detail or reason was chosen)
Susceptible to receiving impurity; they catch טומאה easily
Let him derive it from (a simpler source or reason)
There is nothing else (left as an option)

phrases.english: Why specifically liquids
phrases.notes: Refers to the ברייתא's statement that food makes liquids impure.

phrases.english: because they are susceptible to receiving impurity?
Let him derive it
from the fact that there is nothing else (for food to make impure)!
phrases.notes: Food does not make food impure, and the קל וחומר showed it does not make a כלי impure. So only liquids remain.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אִירְיָא מַשְׁקִין מִשּׁוּם דַּעֲלוּלִין לְקַבֵּל טוּמְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the reason given inside the ברייתא's conclusion in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reason 'liquids are susceptible' in רבי עקיבא's derivation
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Once the other options are ruled out, liquids are the only thing left. A special reason seems unneeded.

steps.title: The reason blocks a mistaken argument from strictness
steps.stepSummary: The reason is needed to stop a wrong argument. Someone might say food's טומאה is strong because it makes liquids impure, so it should also make a כלי impure. The answer: the strictness belongs to the liquids, not to the food.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he means: you might say food is strict, since it makes liquids impure, so let it also make a כלי impure. No. That strictness comes from the liquids, because liquids are susceptible to impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the 'susceptible' reason is needed. It stops a mistaken idea that food is 'strong' enough to make a כלי impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without this reason, one could argue: food makes liquids impure, even though liquids do not make other liquids impure, so food must be stronger than liquids and could make a כלי impure. The answer moves the strictness to the receiver. Liquids catch טומאה easily, so food making them impure proves nothing about food's strength.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he means (explains the true intent)
And if you would say (brings up a possible mistaken idea)
Strict, severe
A stringency, a strict quality

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think food's טומאה is 'stronger' because it affects liquids. The point is the opposite: liquids are 'weaker' at resisting טומאה.

phrases.english: This is what he is saying:
And if you would say that food is strict,
since it makes liquids impure,
phrases.notes: Liquids do not make other liquids impure, so food might look stronger than liquids.

phrases.english: then let it make a vessel impure.
That is a stringency of the liquids,
because liquids are susceptible to receiving impurity.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר: וְכִי תֵּימָא אוֹכֶל חָמוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 8 by showing that the reason has a real purpose.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of purpose: the reason blocks a counter-argument
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Food making liquids impure shows food's טומאה is strong, so it should make a כלי impure.
steps.terutzMaskana: The strictness belongs to the liquids, which catch טומאה easily. Food is not proven strong, so it does not make a כלי impure.

steps.title: How are liquids susceptible?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what exactly makes liquids 'susceptible' to טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is their susceptibility?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a short definition. It asks what 'liquids are susceptible' actually means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole answer in step 9 depends on the word עלולין. So the גמרא pauses to define it concretely.

keyTerms.meaning: Their susceptibility, their tendency to catch טומאה

phrases.english: And what is their susceptibility?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a definition of the key term used in step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What concretely makes liquids more susceptible to טומאה than other items

steps.title: Liquids need no הכשר to become impure
steps.stepSummary: Liquids become impure without needing a הכשר first. Food, by contrast, must first get wet to become able to receive טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: That they receive impurity without being made ready (הכשר).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defines 'susceptible.' Liquids can become impure right away, with no preparation step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food can only become impure after it has been made wet by one of the special liquids. This is called הכשר. Liquids skip this step entirely, which shows they catch טומאה easily.

keyTerms.meaning: Making food ready to receive טומאה, by getting it wet with certain liquids
Without a preparation step

steps.whatToRemember: Food makes liquids impure only because liquids catch טומאה easily, needing no הכשר. It is not because food's טומאה is strong. So food cannot make a כלי impure.

phrases.english: that they receive impurity without being made ready (הכשר).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the definition question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Liquids become impure without needing a prior הכשר.

steps.title: This rule is already taught by another פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why ״יִטְמָא״ is needed to teach that impurity does not pass to a similar item. The פסוק ״וְכִי יֻתַּן מַיִם עַל זֶרַע״ already teaches this with the words 'הוּא טָמֵא'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is the rule that ״יִטְמָא״ teaches, that it does not make a similar item impure, learned from here? It is learned from there: ״But if water is put on seed and some of their carcass falls on it, it is impure.״ It is impure, but it does not make a similar item impure!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new challenge. It points out that the same rule seems to be taught twice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ״יִטְמָא״ in our פסוק is read as 'it becomes impure, but it does not pass טומאה to an item like itself.' But in the פסוק about seed, 'הוּא טָמֵא' ('it is impure') is already read the same way. The Torah does not repeat a lesson for nothing, so why do we need both?

keyTerms.meaning: Something similar to it, of the same type
Is it derived from here?
It is derived from there (another source)
Their carcass (of the שרצים)

phrases.english: ״Shall be impure״, teaching that it does not make something like it impure,
is that derived from here?
It is derived from there:
״But if water is put upon seed
and some of their carcass falls on it, it is impure״
'It' is impure,
phrases.notes: The word 'הוּא' limits it: only the item itself is impure.

phrases.english: but it does not make something like it impure!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the source of the premise used in step 6, that food does not make similar food impure. It asks whether that premise really comes from ״יִטְמָא״ when another פסוק already teaches it.
steps.kashyaTarget: Using ״יִטְמָא״ as the source that impurity does not pass to a similar item
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another פסוק already teaches the same rule, so ״יִטְמָא״ seems unnecessary for this.

steps.title: Two cases: impurity from a שרץ and from a כלי
steps.stepSummary: Both פסוקים are needed because they cover different cases. One covers liquids that got their טומאה from a שרץ. The other covers liquids that got their טומאה from a כלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: One is about liquids that come (to impurity) because of a שרץ, and one is about liquids that come (to impurity) because of a כלי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two sources are not a repeat. Each one teaches the rule for a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The seed פסוק describes a שרץ falling directly on the wet item. Our פסוק is in the context of a כלי that became impure from a שרץ, so there the טומאה came through a כלי. Since the source of the טומאה differs, we could not learn one case from the other, so both פסוקים are needed.

keyTerms.meaning: One... and one (each source covers a different case)
Because of, on account of
A creeping creature whose carcass gives טומאה

steps.whatToRemember: The rule that impurity does not pass to a similar item is taught twice. One source covers liquids made impure by a שרץ, and the other covers liquids made impure by a כלי.

phrases.english: One is about liquids that come to impurity because of a creeping creature,
and one is about liquids that come to impurity because of a vessel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves step 12 by assigning each פסוק to a different case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing cases: each source covers a different case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both פסוקים teach the identical rule, so one is redundant.
steps.terutzMaskana: One פסוק covers liquids made impure by a שרץ, the other covers liquids made impure by a כלי, so both are needed.

steps.title: Why both cases are needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why one פסוק could not have taught us both cases. If only the כלי case were written, we might think the stricter שרץ case is different.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both are needed. If the Torah had taught us only about liquids that became impure from a כלי, we would say they cannot make similar items impure because their טומאה is not severe. But liquids that became impure from a שרץ have severe טומאה, so we might say they do make a similar item impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the answer from the last step. It shows why the Torah needed to teach both cases separately.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Liquids impure from a כלי are a weaker case, because a כלי is not a primary source of טומאה. If the Torah had taught only that weaker case, we might think the rule depends on the weakness. Then we would wrongly say that liquids impure from a שרץ, a primary source, can pass טומאה to a similar item.

keyTerms.meaning: And both are needed. This is the standard opening of a צריכותא, which explains why two sources are necessary.
Because of a vessel. The liquid got its טומאה from touching an impure כלי.
Because of a creeping animal. The liquid got its טומאה from touching a שרץ, a primary source of טומאה.
They are severe or strict.
Something similar to it, meaning another item of the same kind.

phrases.english: And both are needed.
phrases.notes: Opens the explanation of why both פסוקים are necessary.

phrases.english: For if it had taught us only
about liquids that became impure because of a vessel,
I would say the rule applies because they are not severe.
But liquids that became impure because of a creeping animal,
which are severe,
I might say they do make a similar item impure.
phrases.notes: This is the mistaken idea the second פסוק prevents.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer from step 13 by showing why each case needs its own פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: each source covers a case the other could not teach.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: From the כלי case alone, we might think liquids impure from a severe שרץ do pass טומאה to a similar item.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each case needs its own פסוק.

steps.title: Why not write only the stricter case?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the explanation. The Torah could have written only the severe שרץ case, and we would learn the כלי case through a קל וחומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let the Torah teach us only about liquids that became impure from a שרץ. Then we would know all the more so about liquids that became impure from a כלי!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the explanation it just gave. It says one פסוק should have been enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If even the strong שרץ-liquids cannot make a similar item impure, then surely the weaker כלי-liquids cannot either. That is a simple קל וחומר. So the פסוק about the כלי case seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: But let it teach us. This introduces a suggestion that one source would have been enough.
All the more so.

phrases.english: But let it teach us only
about liquids that became impure because of a creeping animal,

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל שֶׁכֵּן מַשְׁקִין הַבָּאִין מֵחֲמַת כְּלִי!
phrases.english: and all the more so we would know about liquids that became impure because of a vessel!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the explanation in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 14 that both פסוקים are needed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The weaker case can be learned from the stronger one through a קל וחומר, so the second פסוק looks extra.

steps.title: The Torah sometimes writes what a קל וחומר could teach
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that sometimes the Torah takes the trouble to write something out, even when a קל וחומר could have taught it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Something that could be learned through a קל וחומר, the Torah sometimes still takes the trouble to write.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It accepts that a קל וחומר was possible, but says the Torah wrote the case anyway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer does not deny the קל וחומר. Instead, it says the Torah sometimes spells out a case on purpose, even when we could have figured it out. So an extra-looking פסוק is not always a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: A logical argument from a weaker case to a stronger one, or the reverse.
The פסוק took the trouble and wrote it anyway.

steps.whatToRemember: Both פסוקים are needed because they cover two different cases. Even though the כלי case could come from a קל וחומר, the Torah sometimes writes such a case out anyway.

phrases.english: A matter that could be learned through a קל וחומר
the verse took the trouble and wrote it anyway.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִילְּתָא דְּאָתְיָא בְּקַל וָחוֹמֶר טָרַח וְכָתֵב לַהּ קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: General principle: the Torah sometimes writes out what a קל וחומר could teach.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A case that a קל וחומר can teach should not get its own פסוק.
steps.terutzMaskana: The Torah sometimes writes such a case anyway, so the second פסוק is fine.

steps.title: רבינא cites רבא against רב אשי
steps.stepSummary: רבינא begins a challenge to רב אשי. He quotes רבא, who said that רבי יוסי does not agree with רבי עקיבא, and רבי עקיבא does not agree with רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: But didn't רבא say that רבי יוסי does not hold like רבי עקיבא, and רבי עקיבא does not hold like רבי יוסי?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא challenges רב אשי's approach by quoting רבא, who said רבי יוסי and רבי עקיבא disagree with each other. רב אשי answers in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said these two תנאים disagree in both directions. רבי יוסי does not accept רבי עקיבא's view about שלישי in חולין. רבי עקיבא does not accept רבי יוסי's view about רביעי in קודשים. If רבי יוסי reads ״יִטְמָא״ like רבי עקיבא to make liquid טומאה a Torah law, he should also accept רבי עקיבא's שלישי in חולין, since that rule comes from the same word.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't he say? This brings an earlier statement as a challenge.
An אמורא who often discusses with רב אשי.
Third level of טומאה.

steps.confusionAlert: רבא's statement is about levels of טומאה (שלישי in חולין, רביעי in קודש), not directly about liquids. The challenge works because, for רבי עקיבא, both rules come from the same word ״יִטְמָא״. רב אשי's answer comes in step 18.

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi:
But didn't Rava say:

phrases.aramaic: לָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי סָבַר כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei does not hold like Rabbi Akiva,
phrases.notes: About third-level טומאה in non-sacred food.

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא סָבַר כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי!
phrases.english: and Rabbi Akiva does not hold like Rabbi Yosei!
phrases.notes: About fourth-level טומאה in holy food.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִינָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי: וְהָא אָמַר רָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the צריכותא discussion to a new challenge against רב אשי's view of רבי יוסי.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's view that, for רבי יוסי, liquid טומאה is a Torah law learned from ״יִטְמָא״.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא said רבי יוסי does not hold like רבי עקיבא. Reading ״יִטְמָא״ the way רבי עקיבא does would force רבי יוסי to accept רבי עקיבא's rule of שלישי in חולין as well.

steps.title: רבי יוסי was only explaining his teacher's view
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers רבינא. רבי יוסי said his statement according to the approach of his teacher רבי עקיבא, but רבי יוסי himself does not hold that way.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: רבי יוסי said it according to the approach of רבי עקיבא, his teacher, but he himself does not hold that way.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the challenge from Step 17. He explains that רבי יוסי was only saying what his teacher רבי עקיבא would hold, not what רבי יוסי holds himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא had pointed out a problem. רבא said that רבי יוסי does not agree with רבי עקיבא, so how could רב אשי use רבי יוסי to support a view that fits רבי עקיבא? רב אשי answers that this statement of רבי יוסי was only 'according to רבי עקיבא.' So the statement does not show what רבי יוסי really thinks. That means it does not clash with רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the approach (system of thinking) of
His teacher
He does not hold this way

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי יוסי changed his mind. He was explaining what the law would be according to his teacher's approach. His own opinion stays different.

phrases.english: He (Rav Ashi) said to him:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּשִׁיטַת רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא רַבּוֹ אֲמָרָהּ,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said it according to the approach of Rabbi Akiva, his teacher,
phrases.notes: He was explaining his teacher's system, not giving his own ruling.

phrases.english: but he himself does not hold that way.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּשִׁיטַת רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא רַבּוֹ אֲמָרָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבינא's challenge from Step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-attribution: the statement only reflects the teacher's view, not the speaker's own view.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רבי יוסי's statement showed his own opinion, which would clash with רבא's claim that he disagrees with רבי עקיבא.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוסי was only stating רבי עקיבא's view. He himself disagrees, so there is no clash with רבא.

steps.title: רב אשי asks רב כהנא about רבא's statement
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says to רב כהנא: I understand that רבי יוסי does not agree with רבי עקיבא, because a ברייתא shows it. He then starts quoting that ברייתא, where רבי יוסי asks how we know that holy food at the fourth level of טומאה is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to רב כהנא: I understand that רבי יוסי does not hold like רבי עקיבא, as a ברייתא teaches: רבי יוסי said, from where do we know that a fourth level in holy food is פסול?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי opens a new question about רבא's statement, using the word 'בשלמא' ('I understand this part'). This is a setup line. He accepts one half of רבא's statement and begins bringing a ברייתא as proof for that half.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's statement had two halves: רבי יוסי does not agree with רבי עקיבא, and רבי עקיבא does not agree with רבי יוסי. רב אשי says the first half is clear from a ברייתא where רבי יוסי works out רביעי בקודש in his own way. The word 'בשלמא' signals that the second half is the real question, and it will come next.

keyTerms.meaning: I understand this part (the other part is the problem)
As it was taught in a ברייתא
From where do we know?
Fourth level of טומאה
Holy food, such as קרבנות
Disqualified (it cannot be eaten, but it does not pass טומאה on)

steps.confusionAlert: 'בשלמא' does not mean the גמרא has finished. It means: 'this half I understand, but the other half is hard.' The hard half comes next.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי לְרַב כָּהֲנָא:
phrases.english: Rav Ashi said to Rav Kahana:

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁלָמָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי לָא סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא,
phrases.english: Granted, Rabbi Yosei does not hold like Rabbi Akiva,
phrases.notes: This is the first half of רבא's statement, which רב אשי accepts.

phrases.english: as it was taught in a baraita: Rabbi Yosei said:
From where do we know that a fourth level in holy food is disqualified?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי לְרַב כָּהֲנָא: בִּשְׁלָמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to רבא's statement quoted in Step 17 and begins to check both of its halves.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How do we know each half of רבא's statement? The first half is supported here; the second half will be asked about next.

steps.title: רבי יוסי's קל וחומר for the fourth level in holy food
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי proves with a קל וחומר that holy food can become a רביעי. A מחוסר כפורים may eat תרומה, yet he makes קודש פסול. A שלישי makes תרומה פסול, so it should surely make קודש into a רביעי.
steps.simpleTranslation: This can be shown by logic: A מחוסר כפורים is allowed to eat תרומה, yet he makes קודש פסול. A שלישי makes תרומה פסול. Is it not logical that it should make קודש into a רביעי?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues. רבי יוסי gives his proof, a קל וחומר, that holy food can reach a fourth level of טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Compare two things. A מחוסר כפורים is weaker, because he does not ruin תרומה. Even so, he ruins קודש. A שלישי is stronger, because it does ruin תרומה. So it should certainly affect קודש and make it a רביעי.

keyTerms.meaning: It is logical (introduces a קל וחומר)
Someone who went to the מקוה but has not yet brought his atonement קרבן
Holy portion given to a כהן; less holy than קודש
Third level of טומאה

phrases.english: And it is a logical inference:
Just as one who lacks atonement,
who is permitted to eat teruma,
disqualifies holy food,
phrases.notes: This is the weaker side of the comparison.

phrases.english: then a third level, which disqualifies teruma,
phrases.notes: This is the stronger side of the comparison.

phrases.english: is it not logical that it should make a fourth level in holy food?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִין הוּא: וּמָה מְחוּסַּר כִּפּוּרִים שֶׁמּוּתָּר בִּתְרוּמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא and answers the 'מניין' question asked in Step 19.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that קודש can become a רביעי, which is part of the evidence that רבי יוסי has his own approach, separate from רבי עקיבא's.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from מחוסר כפורים to שלישי.

steps.title: Third level from the Torah, fourth level from the קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא sums up. שלישי בקודש comes straight from the Torah, and רביעי בקודש comes from the קל וחומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: So we have learned שלישי בקודש from the Torah, and רביעי בקודש from a קל וחומר.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא wraps up by naming the source for each level of טומאה in קודש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a rule called דיו: a קל וחומר normally cannot teach more than its source. One might think it should only teach שלישי, not רביעי. But שלישי בקודש is already written in the Torah. If the קל וחומר only taught שלישי, it would teach nothing new. So here דיו does not limit it, and the קל וחומר teaches רביעי.

keyTerms.meaning: And so we have learned
Straight from a פסוק
Logic from a lighter case to a stricter case

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי יוסי: שלישי בקודש comes from a פסוק, and רביעי בקודש comes from a קל וחומר. רב אשי accepts that רבי יוסי does not hold like רבי עקיבא. The open question is the other half: how do we know רבי עקיבא does not hold like רבי יוסי?
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next move. Once we see how רבי יוסי derives these levels, the גמרא will ask how we know רבי עקיבא disagrees with him.

phrases.english: And we have learned a third level in holy food from the Torah,
and a fourth level from an a fortiori inference.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sums up the sources behind the קל וחומר in Step 20.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For holy food, the third level comes from the Torah and the fourth level comes from the קל וחומר.

steps.title: The Torah source for third-level טומאה in holy food begins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts proving that קודש can become a שלישי from the Torah. It quotes the פסוק "וְהַבָּשָׂר אֲשֶׁר יִגַּע", about holy meat that touches something טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The fact that holy food can become a שלישי comes from the Torah, as it is written: "And the meat that touches..."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is now backing up the ברייתא's summary line by bringing the actual פסוק that teaches שלישי בקודש. This step only begins the quote. The rest of the פסוק and how it is learned come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 21 the ברייתא only stated that שלישי בקודש is מן התורה. Here the גמרא starts giving the proof: a פסוק that says holy meat which touches anything טמא may not be eaten. Even meat that touched a שני, which leaves the meat as a שלישי, is included, so a שלישי in קודש is פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: Third level of טומאה, an item that touched a שני
From the Torah itself, not a רבנן rule or a logical derivation
As it is written, the formula that introduces a פסוק
"And the meat that touches", the start of the פסוק about holy meat

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two sources. Only שלישי בקודש comes from this פסוק. רביעי בקודש comes from the קל וחומר of רבי יוסי in step 20, not from this פסוק.
steps.whyThisMatters: This finishes the ברייתא's two-part structure. The Torah gives us שלישי בקודש, and רבי יוסי's קל וחומר builds on that to reach רביעי בקודש. That is why the ברייתא shows the Torah source for שלישי first.

phrases.english: A third level of impurity in holy food is from the Torah,
phrases.notes: This picks up the first half of the ברייתא's summary in step 21.

phrases.english: as it is written: "And the meat that touches
phrases.notes: This is from ויקרא ז:יט. The פסוק goes on to say that meat touching anything טמא may not be eaten. The quote continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands step 21's summary by supplying the פסוק behind 'שלישי בקודש מן התורה'.
steps.raayaObject: That קודש can become a שלישי on a Torah level.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק "וְהַבָּשָׂר אֲשֶׁר יִגַּע בְּכָל טָמֵא לֹא יֵאָכֵל" (ויקרא ז:יט), quoted partially on this amud.
